newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end higher amid political worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end higher amid political worries.

text.p: Thai stocks ended up in moderate trade on Thursday amid several political rumours as discussions continued over who would be names as the new prime minister, brokers said.
The SET index ended 7.86 points higher at 1,042.80 on 3.9 billion baht trade. Gainers led decliners 228 to 77 while 98 issues unchanged. The SET-50 index was 0.67 point up to 79.64.
"The index moved in a narrow range as investors carefully bought blue-chip shares despite rumours in the market," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance and Securites.

Political uncertainty has hovered over the market since Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa said on Saturday that he would step down in seven days after choosing an appropiate successor. The resignation was in exchange for support from coalition partners in a no-confidence vote.

Rumours emerged again today that former prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan, leader of opposition Chart Pattana party, would be nominated to succeed Banharn if the ruling coalition could not agree on the successor, brokers said.
Brokers said key economic figures, released by the central bank in the afternoon, did not have much impact on the market.
The Bank of Thailand released current account, trade deficit and other indicators before the market reopened in the afternoon.
"The (economic) figures were in line with investors earlier expectations and that's why it didn't move the market," said Thanadech.

Large capitalised stocks rose on speculative buying on Thursday. Bangkok Bank topped the active list in terms of value, gaining two to 218. General Finance and Securities advanced 1.50 to 63 while GCN Finance rose 0.50 to 25.25 but down 2.75 from its IPO price of 28 baht.-- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
